def-qft-positive-tempered-moments:
## Definition

Use the Schwartz spaces and their seminorm topologies of
[[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]] and
[[def-schwartz-topology-and-convergence]]. Put
$S:=\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C)$ and
$S_n:=\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{4n};\mathbb C)$ for $n\ge1$, and set
$S_0:=\mathbb C$. A tempered distribution in $S_n'$ means a continuous
complex-linear functional on $S_n$
as in [[def-tempered-distribution]]; its pairing with a test is bilinear.

For complex vector spaces $S$, let $S^{\otimes_{\rm alg} n}$ be the algebraic
tensor product, characterized by multilinear maps out of $S^n$, with
$S^{\otimes_{\rm alg}0}:=\mathbb C1$. Define the algebraic tensor test algebra
$$T(S):=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}^{\rm alg}S^{\otimes_{\rm alg}n},$$
where the direct sum consists of finite-support sequences. Its multiplication
is concatenation of tensor factors, extended bilinearly, and its unit is $1$
in degree zero. Its conjugate-linear involution is specified on elementary
tensors by
$$(f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_n)^*:=\overline{f_n}\otimes\cdots\otimes\overline{f_1},\qquad (c1)^*=\overline c1.$$

For $f_j\in S$, the elementary tensor is evaluated against a distribution by
the test function
$$J_n(f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_n)(x_1,\ldots,x_n):=\prod_{j=1}^n f_j(x_j).$$
This is in $S_n$: for multi-indices split into four-coordinate blocks
$(\alpha_j,\beta_j)$, its Schwartz seminorm is
$$p_{(\alpha_j)_j,(\beta_j)_j}(J_n(f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_n))=\prod_{j=1}^n p_{\alpha_j\beta_j}(f_j).$$
Thus $J_n$ is multilinear and continuous, and the displayed formula extends
linearly to the algebraic tensor product.
In degree zero set $J_0(c1):=c$.

By these definitions concatenation is associative with the degree-zero unit,
and reversal together with complex conjugation is an involution satisfying
$(ab)^*=b^*a^*$; thus $T(S)$ is a unital complex star algebra.

A **positive tempered moment family** is a sequence consisting of $W_0=1$
and $W_n\in S_n'$ for each $n\ge1$ such that the multilinear maps
$$f_1,\ldots,f_n\longmapsto\langle W_n,J_n(f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_n)\rangle$$
extend, degree by degree and then over finite sums, to a complex-linear
functional $\omega:T(S)\to\mathbb C$ satisfying
$$\omega(1)=1,\qquad \omega(a^*a)\in[0,\infty)\quad(a\in T(S)).$$
Equivalently, the family supplies an actually positive normalized functional
on this algebra. Positivity is a hypothesis on the distributions; formal
coefficient families do not qualify merely because they obey algebraic
identities. No topology on $T(S)$, norm completion, C*-algebra, or existence
claim for an interacting field is part of this definition.
def-qft-weak-operator-valued-tempered-di:
## Definition

Let $S=\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C)$ with its Schwartz topology, let $H$
be a complex Hilbert space, and let $D\subseteq H$ be a dense complex linear
subspace. Use the inner product linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear
in its second, as in [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]. A **weak
operator-valued tempered distribution on the common domain $D$** is a
complex-linear map
$$\Phi:S\longrightarrow\operatorname{Lin}(D),$$
where $\operatorname{Lin}(D)$ is the vector space of linear maps $D\to D$,
such that for every $u,v\in D$ the scalar map
$$f\longmapsto (\Phi(f)u,v)_H$$
is a continuous complex-linear functional on $S$, hence an element of
$S'=\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^4)$ by [[def-tempered-distribution]]. In particular,
every smeared map preserves the same domain $D$. This definition is weak in
the matrix-coefficient sense; it does not define point values $\Phi(x)$,
operators on all of $H$, or self-adjoint closures.
def-qft-poincare-test-action:
## Definition

Fix coordinates $x=(x^0,\mathbf x)\in\mathbb R^4$ and the Minkowski matrix
$$\eta:=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1).$$
The proper-orthochronous Lorentz group is
$$SO^+(1,3):=\{\Lambda\in GL_4(\mathbb R):\Lambda^{\mathsf T}\eta\Lambda=\eta,\ \det\Lambda=1,\ \Lambda^0{}_0\ge1\},$$
with its subspace topology from real $4\times4$ matrices. The proper-orthochronous
Poincaré group is the semidirect product
$$P^\uparrow_+:=SO^+(1,3)\ltimes\mathbb R^4,$$
with multiplication $(\Lambda,a)(\Gamma,b)=(\Lambda\Gamma,a+\Lambda b)$,
identity $e=(I,0)$, and affine action $gx=\Lambda x+a$. Its topology is the
product topology on the matrix and translation coordinates.

For $f\in S:=\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C)$ define the pointwise pullback
formula, viewed initially as a smooth function,
$$T_gf(x):=f(g^{-1}x)=f(\Lambda^{-1}(x-a)).$$
On smooth functions this formula obeys $T_gT_h=T_{gh}$ and $T_ef=f$, by the
group law. This definition specifies the formula and conventions; it does not
assert that $T_gf$ belongs to $S$. Translations have the convention
$T_{(I,z)}f(x)=f(x-z)$.

With this signature, $p\cdot z:=p^0z^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf z$,
$\overline V_+:=\{p\in\mathbb R^4:p^0\ge|\mathbf p|\}$ is the closed forward
cone, and $x-y$ is spacelike exactly when
$(x^0-y^0)^2-|\mathbf x-\mathbf y|^2<0$.
def-qft-minkowski-fourier-transform:
## Definition

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), as
required by the Fourier transform suppliers. With $p\cdot z$ from
[[def-qft-poincare-test-action]], for $\psi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4)$ set
$$\mathcal F_M\psi(z):=\int_{\mathbb R^4}e^{-ip\cdot z}\psi(p)\,d^4p.$$
This is a continuous automorphism of Schwartz space. Indeed, if
$\mathcal F_{2\pi}$ is the Euclidean transform
$\mathcal F_{2\pi}\psi(x)=\int e^{-2\pi i x\cdot p}\psi(p)\,d^4p$,
as in [[def-fourier-transform-of-a-tempered-distribution]], then
$$\mathcal F_M\psi(z)=\bigl(\mathcal F_{2\pi}(\psi\circ\eta)\bigr)(z/(2\pi)).$$
The reflection $\eta$ and dilation by $1/(2\pi)$ preserve Schwartz space by
[[lem-invertible-linear-substitutions-preserve-schwartz-space]], and
$\mathcal F_{2\pi}$ is a topological automorphism by
[[cor-fourier-transform-is-a-topological-automorphism-of-schwartz-space]].

For $D\in\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^4)$ define its Minkowski Fourier transform by
bilinear transposition,
$$\langle\widehat D_M,\psi\rangle:=\langle D,\mathcal F_M\psi\rangle\qquad(\psi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4)).$$
For a closed set $C\subseteq\mathbb R^4$, the statement
$\operatorname{supp}\widehat D_M\subseteq C$ means
$\langle\widehat D_M,\psi\rangle=0$ for every compactly supported smooth
$\psi$ whose support is disjoint from $C$; the inclusion
$C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^4)\hookrightarrow\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4)$ is
[[lem-test-function-inclusion-in-schwartz-space-is-continuous]]. In particular,
the forward-cone condition means $C=\overline V_+$ with the definition in
[[def-qft-poincare-test-action]]. No joint self-adjoint energy-momentum
generators are included in this convention.
lem-qft-poincare-pullback-continuity-on-:
## Statement

For every $g\in P^\uparrow_+$, the pullback $T_gf(x)=f(g^{-1}x)$ of
[[def-qft-poincare-test-action]] maps $S=\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C)$
continuously to itself. For each fixed $f\in S$, the map
$g\mapsto T_gf$ from $P^\uparrow_+$ to $S$ is continuous. Consequently,
$\alpha_g(f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_n):=T_gf_1\otimes\cdots\otimes T_gf_n$
extends algebraically to a unital star-automorphism of the algebraic tensor
test algebra [[def-qft-positive-tempered-moments]], and
$\alpha_g\alpha_h=\alpha_{gh}$. No topology on the algebraic direct sum is
asserted.
thm-qft-tempered-field-reconstruction:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let
$(W_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a positive tempered moment family on $T(S)$ as in
[[def-qft-positive-tempered-moments]]. Write $\omega$ for its linear extension,
and let $P^\uparrow_+$, $T_g$, and $\alpha_g$ be the group and pullbacks of
[[def-qft-poincare-test-action]] and
[[lem-qft-poincare-pullback-continuity-on-schwartz]]. Let
$(H_\omega,D_\omega,\pi_\omega,\Omega_\omega)$ be the GNS construction of
[[thm-qft-algebraic-gns-domain]] for this functional, with the first-variable-
linear Hilbert pairing.

For $f\in S$, put $X(f):=f$ in degree one and
$\Phi(f):=\pi_\omega(X(f))|_{D_\omega}$. Then $D_\omega$ is a common invariant
dense domain, every $\Phi(f)$ is closable with
$\Phi(\overline f)=\Phi(f)^*|_{D_\omega}$, and $\Phi$ is a weak
operator-valued tempered distribution in the exact sense of
[[def-qft-weak-operator-valued-tempered-distribution]]. Its vacuum moments are
exactly the input:
$$\bigl(\Phi(f_1)\cdots\Phi(f_n)\Omega_\omega,\Omega_\omega\bigr)=\langle W_n,J_n(f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_n)\rangle.$$

The following additional conclusions are conditional on additional moment
identities.

1. If $\omega\circ\alpha_g=\omega$ for every $g\in P^\uparrow_+$, then there
is a strongly continuous unitary representation $g\mapsto U_g$ on
$H_\omega$ fixing $\Omega_\omega$ and satisfying
$$U_g\Phi(f)U_g^{-1}|_{D_\omega}=\Phi(T_gf)\qquad(g\in P^\uparrow_+,\ f\in S).$$

2. If $f,h\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C)$ have spacelike-separated
supports, meaning $(x^0-y^0)^2-|\mathbf x-\mathbf y|^2<0$ for every
$x\in\operatorname{supp}f$, $y\in\operatorname{supp}h$, and
$$\omega\bigl(b^*[X(f),X(h)]a\bigr)=0\qquad(a,b\in T(S)),$$
then $[\Phi(f),\Phi(h)]=0$ on $D_\omega$. More generally, any polynomial
relation $r\in T(S)$ satisfying $\omega(b^*ra)=0$ for all $a,b\in T(S)$ is
represented by $\pi_\omega(r)=0$ on $D_\omega$; tested field equations are
instances of this statement when their required identities are assumed.

3. For translations $\tau_z=(I,z)$ define
$$D_{b,a}(z):=\omega\bigl(b^*\alpha_{\tau_z}(a)\bigr)\qquad(a,b\in T(S)).$$
If $\omega$ is translation-invariant, each $D_{b,a}$ is a bounded continuous
function and hence a regular tempered distribution; applying the
symmetry-implementation lemma to the translation subgroup gives strongly
continuous unitaries $U_{\tau_z}$. If, in addition,
$\operatorname{supp}\widehat{D}_{b,a,M}\subseteq\overline V_+$ for every $a,b$,
with the Fourier convention of
[[def-qft-minkowski-fourier-transform]], then the reconstructed translation
matrix coefficients
$$z\longmapsto\bigl(U_{\tau_z}\pi_\omega(a)\Omega_\omega,\pi_\omega(b)\Omega_\omega\bigr)$$
have precisely the same Fourier support. This is a matrix-coefficient
spectrum condition; it does not assert joint self-adjoint energy-momentum
generators or their joint spectral measure.

This theorem reconstructs a weak field only from supplied, actually positive
continuous moments. It does not construct an unspecified positive functional,
complete a formal perturbation series, or establish the full Wightman
reconstruction theorem with assumptions not listed here.
